title: Sharpness and uniqueness for positive solutions of the explicit formula for ζ(s)
description:
Paper (39 pages) with its LaTeX sources and ancillary files (certificate scripts, data files and logs), and a Lean 4 formalisation of the paper's logical spine with its axiom ledger. Part II of a series; Part I is Positive solutions of the explicit formula for ζ(s): near-criticality and uniqueness (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23197915). Preprint, October 2026; not yet peer-reviewed.

Weil's explicit formula for ζ(s) equates a functional 𝒜(F), which depends only on the archimedean data of ζ, with sums over the zeros and over the prime powers. We construct an explicit even function F = Ξ2H, with H entire and positive on ℝ, such that F ≥ 0 and F̂ ≥ 0 on ℝ, F̂ vanishes at log n/(2π) for every integer n ≥ 2, and 𝒜(F) = 0. Since Ξ vanishes at every non-trivial zero, on or off the critical line, no information about the zeros is used. F is an exact magic function, in the sense of the sphere-packing bounds of Cohn–Elkies and Viazovska, for the linear programme of Odlyzko, Poitou and Serre: for the data of ζ the programme has no positive slack, so the method is sharp, and F is a minimiser under RH. With a support theorem of Part I, every pair of positive measures satisfying the formula, on the zero side and on the prime side beyond log 2/(2π), is then ζ's own. This resolves Conjectures S and U of Part I. H comes from an eigenvalue-¼ eigenfunction of the hyperbolic Laplacian through a contour argument of Viazovska's type, with Green's identity in place of Cauchy's theorem; its positivity is partly computer-assisted. We do not prove RH; by these results it is equivalent to the existence of such a pair.

The Lean 4 formalisation (paper/anc/lean) builds on that of Part I, version 1.3 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23217537). It states the main results (Theorems 1 and 2 and Corollary 3) in Lean, with every difference from the paper's statements listed in FAITHFUL.md, and proves them from Mathlib, six axioms of Part I's ledger and an explicit axiom ledger of two axioms of its own (an analytic lemma proved in the paper, and the existence of the object constructed in the paper with its properties; the construction itself is not formalised); it contains no sorry, and its build and audit run in continuous integration.

This paper was produced by AI agents, mainly Anthropic's Claude with supplementary assistance from OpenAI's Astra, under the author's direction; it has not yet been checked by a human expert.
